data.title: Bitcoin.com Launches Tokenized U.S. Stocks and ETF Service for Eligible U.S. Users
data.description:
Bitcoin.com has launched tokenized U.S. stocks and ETF services for eligible users in the United States through Dinari, a tokenized securities infrastructure company. According to Odaily, users can access the assets directly through Bitcoin.com Wallet.

Dinari offers tokenized U.S. stocks and ETFs through dShares and currently supports 724 assets, including all constituents of the S&P 500. Each dShare is directly linked to the corresponding U.S. security held by a licensed custodian.

Bitcoin.com is the first partner to deploy Dinari's Embedded Trading App, allowing users to browse stocks and ETFs, access market data, execute trades, and manage portfolios without leaving the existing product. The infrastructure also supports integration for brokerages, wallets, and fintech platforms.

data.title: Linde Revenue Growth Seen Rising on AI-Driven Semiconductor Demand
data.description: According to CNBC, Linde's revenue growth rate is set to rise to at least 8% as artificial intelligence-related semiconductor manufacturing drives demand for industrial gases, supported by a record $11.1 billion project backlog and major supply agreements near chip fabs. The company said about 30% of its gas revenue comes from on-site facilities protected by 15- to 20-year take-or-pay contracts with energy cost pass-throughs, while operating margins are moving toward 31% and adjusted earnings per share are projected to grow 13% to 14% annually. Linde shares closed Monday at $464.41, and the stock has fallen more than 3% over the past year.

data.title: CBO Says Iran War Could Lift U.S. Inflation by 0.5 Points by Early 2027
data.description:
The U.S. Congressional Budget Office said the Trump administration had spent about $38 billion in the five months before the war with Iran began. According to ChainCatcher, the agency expects the conflict to push up U.S. inflation, with the inflation measure in early 2027 projected to be 0.5 percentage points higher than previously forecast.

The CBO also said replenishing ammunition stocks used in the war could take more than five years, potentially limiting the U.S. ability to respond to other conflicts.

data.title: Thomas Massie to Force House Impeachment Vote on Pete Hegseth
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Republican U.S. Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky will force the House this week to vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over concerns related to the Iran war. Massie, a Judiciary Committee member who is leaving Congress after losing his primary, read the impeachment articles against Hegseth in the House on Tuesday and filed the measure as a privileged motion, which means it will trigger a vote within two legislative days.

data.title: BoE Official Says Dollar Stablecoin Growth Could Reinforce U.S. Dollar Dominance
data.description:
Bank of England Financial Policy Committee member Carolyn Wilkins said the growth of dollar stablecoins could strengthen the U.S. dollar’s global dominance and increase demand for U.S. Treasurys. According to Odaily, she made the remarks during a speech at Queen’s University Belfast and said dollar stablecoins can facilitate cross-border settlement and expand access to dollar assets outside the United States.

Wilkins said Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC held nearly $150 billion in U.S. Treasurys by the end of 2025 and bought about $33 billion during the year. She added that large-scale stablecoin redemptions could force issuers to sell Treasurys, amplifying market volatility.

She also said total stablecoin circulation has exceeded $300 billion, with 98% of its value pegged to the dollar. Wilkins said this gives the dollar a significant first-mover advantage and that stablecoin market development now has implications beyond the crypto sector.

Wilkins said sterling stablecoin development has been slower. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority has used a dedicated regulatory sandbox to test potential issuers, finalized stablecoin issuance rules in June, and the Bank of England has also tested the feasibility of using stablecoins together with a simulated digital pound for cross-border trade payments.

data.title: David Bailey Says AI Could Drive Bitcoin Adoption
data.description:
Nakamoto Holdings CEO and Chairman David Bailey said artificial intelligence could become the next engine for Bitcoin adoption during a discussion hosted by investment bank TD Cowen. According to ChainCatcher, Bailey argued that the main barrier to Bitcoin adoption has been the user interface rather than the asset itself, saying wallets, addresses, private keys, and the onboarding process have kept mainstream users away for more than a decade.

He said AI-powered tools could hide that complexity and make Bitcoin easier for both individuals and institutions to use. TD Cowen analyst Lance Vitanza described the view as speculative but notable, saying it shifts the adoption debate away from traditional topics such as monetary policy, regulation, and institutional inflows.

Bailey also said institutional Bitcoin adoption has only just begun, adding that spot ETFs, corporate treasury plans, and sovereign interest over the past year have changed the market more than the previous decade combined. He said the opportunities ahead remain larger than those already captured.

When asked whether Bitcoin is reshaping traditional finance, Bailey said the answer is yes, noting that institutions, governments, and public companies are participating at scale while Bitcoin's underlying properties remain unchanged. Nakamoto describes itself as a Bitcoin platform spanning media, conferences, education, asset management, advisory, and treasury services. TD Cowen assigned Nakamoto Holdings a Buy rating.
